beliefs.practice: Never hard-code the DOCUMENTDB connection string or credentials: read the MongoDB URI from an environment variable (e.g. DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and do not commit secrets to the repo.

Always enable TLS/SSL for the MongoDB connection string and verify the server certificate; ensure the connection URI uses mongodb+srv or mongodb+ssl as appropriate so traffic to the managed cluster is encrypted in transit.

Use a connection pool (Mongoose/MongoClient default pooling) and reuse a single shared connection across the app instead of opening a new connection per request; set reasonable poolSize/maxPoolSize and serverSelectionTimeoutMS.

When using multi-document transactions, start a session, pass the session into all reads and writes within the transaction, and commit/abort the transaction; do not rely on implicit transactions across collections without an explicit session.

Design idempotency using a unique index on an idempotency key field (e.g. idempotencyKey) and perform an insert/check inside the same transaction or use upsert semantics with handling for duplicate key errors to avoid double-billing.

Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds) on ephemeral entitlement/trial documents and set the TTL field as a date (e.g. expiresAt) so the database will automatically remove expired documents without application cleanup jobs.

Create appropriate indexes for query patterns used by the app (e.g. customerId on chargeEvents, subscriptionId on entitlements, unique index on idempotencyKey) and verify index usage with explain() to avoid collection scans.

Keep transactional scope small and limited to the minimal set of documents that must be updated atomically (e.g. insert chargeEvent + update subscription status), to reduce transaction conflicts and latency.
Implement retry logic for transient network and write errors (with exponential backoff) and be sure to make retries idempotent or protected by the idempotency key to avoid duplicate charges.

Use writeConcern and readConcern settings appropriate for the app: for financial operations prefer majority/acknowledged writes and repeatable reads (where supported) when recording charges and updating subscription state.
Avoid large multi-megabyte transactions or very large documents inside transactions—keep documents small and limit the number of documents touched in a single transaction to maintain performance.
When using Mongoose, explicitly pass the session returned by startSession() into all Model.create(), Model.updateOne(), findOneAndUpdate(), etc., so the operations participate in the transaction.

Validate and canonicalize idempotency keys (length and character set) at the API boundary and persist them with a timestamp and request metadata so you can reliably detect and reject duplicate attempts.

Provision collections and indexes programmatically as part of deployment (scripts or migrations) and verify index creation and query plans against the live cluster rather than relying on implicit index creation at runtime.

Monitor operation metrics, slow queries and index usage (server logs, explain() output and the provider's monitoring tools) and alert on failed transactions, high retry rates, or elevated latency for critical charge flows.

Beware of provider-specific limitations: confirm that the managed MongoDB API supports multi-document transactions, TTL indexes, unique indexes and the specific wire protocol version before relying on them in production.

If using vector search features, create the appropriate vector index type (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) with correct metric/dimension settings on the collection and ensure the server version and provisioning tier support vector indexes before storing embeddings.

Set sensible TTL and retention policies for audit and billing history: keep chargeEvent records for the required compliance window and do not rely on TTL on primary billing/audit records unless retention requirements allow automatic expiry.

Handle duplicate-key error codes (E11000) explicitly in application code as the signal that an idempotent operation has already been performed, and return a 200/409 with the existing result rather than retrying blindly.
Limit privileges of the database user used by the application to the specific database (sample_fintech_16) and minimum required roles; do not run the app with an admin/root user credential.
